input.input_needs_description:
I plan and render the visual reference images for a video: identity sheets for each character/location/prop, scene-level adaptations, and one starting frame per planned shot. I work primarily from a written screenplay.

For each [label] below, find every artifact in the registry whose caption describes the same kind of thing. Use the natural-language caption only — do not match by filename or by any tag. Sources are irrelevant: an image may have come from a user upload or from another agent's run; both are treated identically once their captions semantically match.

[screenplay] (single)
The full unified screenplay document for the story: scenes broken into ordered shots with camera direction, action description, and per-scene consistency information (visual style, color, lighting, characters and locations involved, things to keep, things to avoid). It is the primary creative document defining what shots exist and how they should look. Choose at most one such document.

[character_reference] (collection)
Image artifacts that depict what specific characters in the story should look like. Each entry's caption identifies the character (by name, role, or visual description). When present, I use these as global character anchors in Layer 1 instead of generating from text — I record the resolved image path on the matching character entity so the materializer reads the bytes from disk instead of running text-to-image. When absent, I generate the character anchor from text alone.

[location_reference] (collection)
Image artifacts depicting what specific locations or settings in the story should look like. Same handling as character references — when present, the resolved path is recorded on the matching location entity; when absent, the location is generated from text.

[prop_reference] (collection)
Image artifacts depicting what specific props or objects in the story should look like. Same handling as character references — when present, the resolved path is recorded on the matching prop entity; when absent, the prop is generated from text.

[style_reference] (collection)
Image artifacts conveying overall visual style, mood, palette, or aesthetic that should inform image generation. Unlike character/location references, these don't depict specific entities — they describe how things should look in general. When present, I incorporate them as style guidance in my generation prompts; when absent, the style is inferred from the screenplay's per-scene mood / tone metadata.

llm_call.system_prompt:
You match a sub-agent's input requirements to artifacts in an artifact registry.

The sub-agent's input requirements are written as one or more [label] blocks. Each block has a header of the form
    [label_name] (single)        -- exactly one matching artifact expected
    [label_name] (collection)    -- zero or more matching artifacts expected
followed by a natural-language description of what kind of artifact that label refers to.

The artifact registry lists every persisted artifact with a #N id and a natural-language caption describing its type, pipeline role, and which agent produced it.

Your job:
  1. Read each [label] block and understand the kind of artifact the agent is asking for in that slot.
  2. For each registry artifact, read its caption and understand the artifact's type, role, and purpose. Reason about meaning.
  3. For each [label], decide which artifacts in the registry are instances of the kind described in that block.
  4. Be inclusive for (collection) labels: include EVERY matching artifact, never just a sample.
  5. Be exclusive for (single) labels: pick the single best matching artifact (or none if none clearly fits).
  6. Distinguish artifacts that look superficially similar but play different roles in the pipeline (e.g. a reference image of an entity in isolation vs. a planned frame of a specific shot of the story). Use the caption to decide.
  7. Only return #N ids that appear in the registry.

Return strict JSON only, with this shape:
{
  "selections": {
    "<label_name>": [0, 3, 5],
    ...
  },
  "rationale": "<a short explanation of how you matched each label>"
}
Use exactly the label names from the agent's [label] headers as keys. Values are arrays of integer ids (the #N numbers from the registry).

scenes.summary: 在封神之战的末尾，姜子牙准备在风暴肆虐的封神台上处决最后的九尾狐妖，气氛庄重而压抑。

character_wardrobe_notes.wardrobe: 褴褛的白袍，沾染尘土和血迹
庄严的道士将领服，深色，衬托其威严

environment_notes: 古老的封神台，被暗沉的漩涡状乌云笼罩，不时有神圣的闪电划过，九天雷声轰鸣。气氛悲剧、庄重、压抑，充满中国神话色彩。

identity_notes: 九尾狐妖，战争的最后幸存者，极度恐惧且疲惫，在古代中国神话背景下被处决。
狐妖本体形态为九尾狐。
wardrobe_notes: 破损的白袍，象征其落魄与脆弱。

identity_notes: 姜子牙，冷酷、坚决的道士将领，在古代中国神话背景下执行天命。
wardrobe_notes: 庄严的道士将领服，衬托其权威与职责。

must_keep: 带有神圣符文的巨大长剑，散发威严。

global_style_notes: 悲剧、庄重、压抑、哀伤的中国神话史诗风格，以“封神演义”为背景。

scene_end.turn: 姜子牙已拔出神剑，处决即将开始。
scene_end.emotional_shift: 从绝望的等待转变为极度的恐惧与压迫感。

shots.text: 古老的封神台上，乌云密布，电闪雷鸣。姜子牙身着庄严的道士服，面无表情地矗立着，手按腰间佩剑。

camera.framing_notes: 展现封神台的宏大与压抑，姜子牙身影孤高。

shots.visual_goal: 建立场景的宏大、庄严和压抑气氛，展示姜子牙的威严。
shots.action_focus: 姜子牙的屹立，神台的背景

shots.text: 九尾狐妖被捆缚在石柱上，破损的白袍下身躯瑟瑟发抖。她眼神充满绝望和恐惧，泪水与雨水混合着划过苍白的脸颊。

camera.framing_notes: 聚焦狐妖的脸部和上半身，展现其脆弱与恐惧。

shots.visual_goal: 展现九尾狐妖的绝望与无助，强调其面临的危险。
shots.action_focus: 狐妖的面部表情和身体颤抖

shots.text: 姜子牙缓缓抽出腰间的神圣斩妖剑，剑身在雷电中闪烁着寒光，他眼神坚定，仿佛没有一丝犹豫。

camera.framing_notes: 特写姜子牙的手和剑，彰显其力量与决心。

shots.visual_goal: 突出姜子牙的执行决心和神圣斩妖剑的威慑力。
shots.action_focus: 姜子牙拔剑的动作，剑身的光芒

scenes.summary: 姜子牙高举神剑，九尾狐妖在极度恐惧中，眼前闪现了破碎的记忆，一瞥桃花林中的温柔身影。

identity_notes: 神秘男子，温柔而慰藉，在古代中国神话背景下。他的命运与姜子牙和狐妖紧密相连。
